premises.text: Dev and production environments mismatch, sending engineers down wasteful bug rabbit holes

premises.text: Slow tests leave engineers waiting instead of working
premises.evidence_span: Testing took forever. And when your tests take a long time to run, your engineers essentially are not doing work

premises.text: A build break blocks the whole team and destroys productivity
premises.evidence_span: When a build break happens, your entire team is blocked from doing work

premises.text: Quality isolates each change in limbo so a would-be break never hits the shared build
premises.evidence_span: quality, I mentioned, has this in a limbo state, in isolation. So nobody else has actually seen this change. The build is not broken

premises.text: Every change is tested on multiple production-environment replicas in a customer-chosen cloud, including behind the firewall
premises.evidence_span: it spins up multiple replicas of Jordan's production environment in a cloud system of his choosing

premises.text: The automation test suite is chunked and thrown at replicas in parallel for fast turnaround
premises.evidence_span: it will chunk up your automation test suite, and it'll just throw it at these replicas in parallel

premises.text: Companies that cannot afford Google-scale internal tooling need a buyable product so engineers work on their own problems
premises.evidence_span: They want their engineers working on their problems, moving their companies forward
